title: Coverage-based Greybox Fuzzing as Markov Chain (AFLFast)
direction: MONO-UP in path rarity (FAST: energy ~ 2^s(i)/f(i)); rarity proxies higher local discovery probability, not item difficulty
evidence: Abstract: 'energy is inversely proportional to the density of the stationary distribution'
notes: Not E2: low-frequency paths are under-explored neighbourhoods, so rarity tends to mean HIGHER per-input discovery p (Good-Turing view). f(i) rises as the seed is fuzzed, giving implicit diminishing returns; no explicit discount for infeasible frontiers. Baseline: AFL default schedule. Regime rule for this field: per-seed/per-target new-path, new-bug or target-reach events are coded B (first-discovery Bernoulli trials whose p depletes); program/class-level coverage totals with saturating curves are coded C.

title: Directed Greybox Fuzzing (AFLGo)
direction: MONO-DOWN in difficulty: seeds closer to targets get more energy (simulated annealing)
evidence: paraphrase: energy set by seed-to-target distance under a simulated-annealing schedule
notes: Easier (closer) items get more: correct direction when u*p is small. No discount for unreachable targets.

title: Hawkeye: Towards a Desired Directed Grey-box Fuzzer
direction: MONO-DOWN in difficulty: closer / more target-similar traces get more power
evidence: paraphrase: power schedule from adjacent-function distance and trace similarity

title: Beacon: Directed Grey-Box Fuzzing with Provable Path Pruning
direction: hopeless discount: paths provably unable to reach target get zero effort
evidence: paraphrase: prunes paths failing weakest preconditions before execution
notes: Explicit p=0 discount rather than graded allocation.

title: Boosting Fuzzer Efficiency: An Information Theoretic Perspective (Entropic)
objective: rate of discovery of new features (species)
evidence: Sec.1: 'Entropic assigns more energy to seeds revealing more information about the program behaviors.'
notes: Per-seed local entropy estimates discovery rate (marginal value); Laplace prior gives unfuzzed seeds high energy. Baseline: LibFuzzer default schedule. Regime rule for this field: per-seed/per-target new-path, new-bug or target-reach events are coded B (first-discovery Bernoulli trials whose p depletes); program/class-level coverage totals with saturating curves are coded C.

title: EcoFuzz: Adaptive Energy-Saving Greybox Fuzzing as a Variant of the Adversarial Multi-Armed Bandit
evidence: paraphrase (abstract): avoids wasting energy on seeds exercising frequently-travelled paths
notes: Energy follows a bandit estimate of each seed's reward probability; low-yield seeds discounted.

title: MOPT: Optimized Mutation Scheduling for Fuzzers
evidence: paraphrase: particle-swarm optimisation of operator probabilities from per-operator yield, vs uniform choice
notes: Arm selection for one shared objective rather than separate items.

title: FairFuzz: A Targeted Mutation Strategy for Increasing Greybox Fuzz Testing Coverage
direction: MONO-UP in branch rarity
evidence: Abstract: 'FairFuzz automatically prioritizes inputs exercising rare parts of the program under test.'
notes: E2-candidate, not flagged. Published abstract says rare branches 'often guard code that is empirically hard to cover', i.e. rarity framed as difficulty. But the seed already hits the rare branch, so the frontier beyond it is under-explored and plausibly has higher discovery p. No discount for rare branches whose continuation is infeasible.

title: Scheduling Black-box Mutational Fuzzing
direction: RGR/Density/Rate beliefs: more time to configurations that have shown more bugs (higher p)
evidence: Sec.4: Remaining Probability Mass bounded by 3/N via 'Rule of Three'
notes: Weighted coupon-collector model. RPM = probability that the next run yields a new bug (marginal value); EWT and Rate normalise by time. Baselines: Round-Robin, Uniform-Random. Closest fuzzing analogue of the regime-B principle; reports 1.5x more unique bugs than CERT BFF.

title: Effective Seed Scheduling for Fuzzing with Graph Centrality Analysis (K-Scheduler)
direction: explicitly discounts hard-to-reach edges
evidence: Abstract: count 'should decrease if mutation history information suggests an edge is hard to reach'
notes: Katz centrality over the reachable unvisited frontier is a proxy for future gain, with a hopeless-edge discount.

title: Make out like a (Multi-Armed) Bandit: Improving the Odds of Fuzzer Seed Scheduling with T-Scheduler
evidence: Sec.3: 'Beta-Bernoulli bandit, which we solve with Thompson sampling.'
notes: Posterior over each seed's probability of new behaviour, reweighted by feature rareness; no per-target hyperparameter tuning.

title: Reinforcement Learning-based Hierarchical Seed Scheduling for Greybox Fuzzing (AFL-Hier)
direction: MONO-UP in feature rareness (UCB1 on a rareness reward)
evidence: Sec.IV: 'probability of exercising new coverage is dramatically decreased'
notes: The authors replace the marginal (new-feature) reward with the rareness of the rarest feature hit, because the marginal reward decays to near zero and UCB cannot rank seeds. Rareness falls as hit counts rise, so it is self-discounting. Not flagged E2.

title: SLIME: Program-sensitive Energy Allocation for Fuzzing
evidence: Abstract: allocate more energy to seeds 'that have high efficiency to trigger unique paths'
notes: UCB-V bandit across queues; efficiency = yield rate.

title: AFL++: Combining Incremental Steps of Fuzzing Research
direction: menu of schedules incl. 'rare' (MONO-UP rarity) and explore/exploit variants
evidence: paraphrase: exposes several power schedules (fast, coe, lin, quad, rare, mmopt)
notes: Framework paper; schedules compared empirically rather than derived.

title: autofz: Automated Fuzzer Composition at Runtime
evidence: Sec.1: 'Naive resource allocation results in inefficiency.'
notes: A preparation phase measures each fuzzer's runtime coverage trend (rate); the focus phase reallocates. Baselines: equal-core EnFuzz/CollabFuzz. The preparation phase is spent inside the budget.

title: BandFuzz: An ML-powered Collaborative Fuzzing Framework
evidence: Sec.1: 'multi-arm bandits-powered resource allocation method'

title: Fuzzing at Scale: The Untold Story of the Scheduler
evidence: Sec.3: 'we assign exponentially greater importance to recent fuzzing results'
notes: Baseline allocates equal fuzz time to all programs. A discounted epsilon-greedy MAB on recent coverage rate is a marginal-gain estimate. The final scheduler ('Boian') re-balances over time; parameters are cycled rather than tuned on the evaluation.

title: FishFuzz: Throwing Larger Nets to Catch Deeper Bugs
items: sanitizer targets (up to tens of thousands)
direction: NON-MONO: drops exhausted/unfruitful targets, favours rarely tested ones
evidence: Abstract: 'exhaustively explored targets should be dropped'
notes: Also: 'discards unfruitful targets and priorities rarely tested ones' (Sec.1).

title: Multiple Targets Directed Greybox Fuzzing (LeoFuzz)
objective: reach multiple targets (crash reproduction, bug exposure)
direction: MONO-UP: harder-to-cover target sequences give their seeds more energy
evidence: Sec.III: 'TSi is more difficult to reach, and thus the seed should be assigned more energy'
notes: Difficulty = low global max coverage of the target sequence. No discount for unreachable targets. Clearest E2 in this field.

title: Toward Unbiased Multiple-Target Fuzzing with Path Diversity (AFLRun)
direction: equal weight per target regardless of reachability, motivated by under-served deep targets
evidence: Sec.1: 'deeper target sites may receive insufficient fuzzing effort'
notes: Sec.6.3: 'AFLRUN starts with uniform weight values for all target basic block'. Fairness across targets moves energy toward hard targets relative to distance-averaging; no hopeless-target discount. Flagged E2 by motivation; the mechanism is equal per target, not strictly increasing.

title: Titan: Efficient Multi-target Directed Greybox Fuzzing
direction: MONO-DOWN in difficulty: seeds with higher potential to reach each target first
evidence: Abstract: 'differentiates seeds' potential of reaching each target for the scheduling'
notes: Also rejects infeasible executions (Sec.2).

title: Send Hardest Problems My Way: Probabilistic Path Prioritization for Hybrid Fuzzing (DigFuzz)
direction: MONO-UP: lowest-probability (hardest for the fuzzer) paths go to concolic execution
evidence: Abstract: 'assigns the most difficult paths to concolic execution'
notes: Harder-gets-more, but the resource is a complementary, near-deterministic solver (one solve per branch), so the regime-B argument does not apply; it is a division-of-labour argument. Infeasible paths still use solver time.

title: VUzzer: Application-aware Evolutionary Fuzzing
direction: MONO-UP in block depth (low reach probability); error-handling blocks de-weighted
evidence: paraphrase: deeper low-probability blocks get higher fitness weight; error-handling code de-weighted
notes: Fitness rewards inputs that reached hard blocks (rarity-like). Error-path de-weighting discounts unproductive regions. Not flagged.

title: Cerebro: Context-aware Adaptive Fuzzing for Effective Vulnerability Detection
direction: more energy to seeds covering complex / recently changed code (higher bug prior)
evidence: paraphrase: multi-objective seed ranking and power schedule using complexity and code freshness

title: Regression Greybox Fuzzing (AFLChurn)
direction: more energy to seeds exercising recently / frequently changed code (higher bug prior)
evidence: paraphrase: power schedule from code age and churn, ant-colony style

title: DAFL: Directed Grey-box Fuzzing guided by Data Dependency
direction: MONO-DOWN in difficulty (semantic proximity to target)
evidence: paraphrase: energy from a semantic relevance score on a thin-slice data-dependency graph

title: MobFuzz: Adaptive Multi-objective Optimization in Gray-box Fuzzing
evidence: paraphrase: a bandit picks the objective combination; energy by multi-objective optimisation

title: Adaptive Grey-Box Fuzz-Testing with Thompson Sampling
evidence: Abstract: operators 'selected uniformly at random in AFL' vs a learned distribution
notes: Arm selection, not separate items.

title: An Adaptive Search Budget Allocation Approach for Search-Based Test Case Generation (BOT)
evidence: Abstract: 'allocating a fixed search budget for all the components is not recommended'
notes: Predicts each class's coverage-vs-budget curve (BRANCHOS, trained on separate data) and adds budget greedily by cost-effectiveness (Sec.4 example: +5 s gives +5 branches). Baseline: Campos et al., budget proportional to #branches.

title: Continuous Test Generation: Enhancing Continuous Integration with Automated Test Generation
direction: budget proportional to class size (#branches); history: changed / under-covered classes get more
evidence: via BOT Sec.2: 'proportionally divides the search budget based on the number of branches'
notes: Proportional to potential gain b_i (exponent 1 vs optimal 1/(1+alpha)): E3-like, but the signal is size, not spread, so not flagged. Coded from a secondary description.

title: Defect Prediction Guided Search-Based Software Testing (SBST_CL)
direction: MONO-DOWN in difficulty: more time to classes with higher predicted defect probability
evidence: via Perera et al. 2021: 'allocate a higher time budget to highly likely to be defective classes'
notes: Higher-p items get more: the right direction at small u*p.

title: STADS: Software Testing as Species Discovery
exclude_reason: estimation framework (Good-Turing discovery probability); no allocation across items. Used as prior work.

title: Fuzzing: On the Exponential Cost of Vulnerability Discovery
exclude_reason: empirical scaling of discovery vs resources; no allocation. Prior work.

title: Estimating Residual Risk in Greybox Fuzzing
exclude_reason: estimator of discovery probability; no allocation comparison

title: Seed Selection for Successful Fuzzing
exclude_reason: initial-corpus minimisation, not budget allocation across items
